newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso seen higher on IMF support.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso seen higher on IMF support.

text.p: The Philippine peso is likely to gain ground on Tuesday with an additional $710 million from the IMF to shore up the central bank's foreign currency reserves, traders said.
"It would be an appreciating peso. There's the psychological impact on the market," a trader said, referring to the IMF money.
The central bank has more money to intervene, which should prod those with dollars to unload before the peso further appreciates, the trader said, adding the peso may touch 28.
The peso closed at 28 on Monday but hit a day-low of 28.5.
Central bank governor Gabriel Singson said in a television programme late on Monday the central bank's gross international reserves will go up to $10.45 billion with the IMF money.
Other traders believe the peso could still weaken to 28.50 since some banks are still short of dollars to meet clients' requirements.
